threads.thread_goal: Align on current procedures and confirm scope of the integrated support programme.

messages.text: Hi team, welcome to the Early Support Pilot project. We're here to design a coordinated programme for at-risk children across school and community. Let's start by understanding how we currently identify and refer children who need extra support. Can everyone share their current process? I'll kick off: in my experience, we often spot concerns during classroom time, but the handoff to social services isn't always smooth. Looking forward to mapping this out together with A1 and T1.

Good to be here. From the classroom side, we're already doing informal observations—watching for behaviour changes, learning gaps, signs of stress. But we don't have a structured checklist, so it's inconsistent across classes. I think T3 on the observation checklist will be key. What I'm wondering is: how do we make sure the social work team actually gets the information they need without overwhelming them?

That's exactly the gap we need to close. On the social services side, we rely on school referrals, but they come in different formats and sometimes lack detail. We also do home assessments, but there's no clear protocol for when that's triggered. I think we need to define roles and steps clearly in T2—the referral protocol. Let me ask: are there any safeguarding or data protection rules we need to bake in from day one?

Yes, safeguarding is non-negotiable. We need consent from parents before sharing any information, and we have to follow data protection rules strictly. I've worked with both school and social work teams, and I can tell you: if we don't get this right, we'll lose trust. I'd suggest we include a clear consent section in A2 and make sure everyone gets trained on it. Should we also define what counts as 'at-risk' so we're all using the same criteria?

Good point on criteria. I think we should start with the current procedures mapping—T1—to see what we're already doing, then build the protocol from there. I can help with that, but I'll need input from both sides. Maybe we could set up a quick call to walk through the existing processes? I'm thinking we document what school does, what social services does, and where the gaps are.

I can support that. Though I should mention—I'm still getting up to speed on some of the social work side, so I'll need a bit of guidance. But I can definitely help pull together what we're doing in the classroom. One thing I'm concerned about: we have limited time (21 days), so we need to move quickly. How many classes are we thinking for the pilot? That'll affect how much we can realistically do.

Good question. I'd suggest we start with 2–3 classes to keep it manageable. That gives us enough data to learn without overloading staff. We should also think about which families are likely to engage—that'll affect our home visit planning. I think T9 should outline the pilot scope and timeline. Should we aim to start in the next week or two?

Two to three classes sounds right. I'd lean toward starting within 10 days if we can get the protocol and checklist ready. That gives us time to train staff and still have a full term for the pilot. Let me propose: I'll draft T2 (the referral protocol) by end of week, and 350111 can lead T1 (current procedures mapping) with input from both school and social work. Does that work?

I can take that on. I'll set up a shared doc and start filling in what we do on the school side. I'll need someone from social services to add their processes. 361403, can you help with that part? And I'll make sure to flag any gaps or overlaps as I go.

Absolutely. I'll add the social services side and review what you've documented. We should also think about A7—the pilot plan and schedule. Once we have the scope locked in, we can finalize that. So to summarize: we're aiming for 2–3 classes, starting within 10 days, and we'll have T1 and T2 ready by end of week. Does everyone agree on that timeline?

I'm on board. One more thing: we should make sure the observation checklist (T3) is ready at the same time, so teachers know what to look for. I can draft that if 511446 wants to review it for practicality. We need it to be quick—no more than 5 minutes per child.

Happy to review. I've done a lot of classroom observation work, so I can make sure it's realistic for busy days. Let's keep it focused on the key signs—behaviour, learning, safety. I'll give feedback once you have a draft.

Sounds good. So we have a plan: T1 and T2 by end of week, T3 draft soon after. I'll help where I can, though I'm still learning the social work side of things. Let me know if you need anything from the classroom perspective.

Great. I think we've got a solid starting point. Let me recap the decisions: we're going with 2–3 classes for the pilot, starting within 10 days. 350111 is leading T1 with 361403's input, and 361403 is drafting T2. 499701 will draft T3 with 511446's review. Does that capture it?

Perfect. I'll also start thinking about A2 and the safeguarding angle. One thing I want to flag: we need to make sure the protocol aligns with existing school procedures—that's part of T11. We should check in with school leadership early to avoid surprises. I'll include that in my draft.

Good thinking. School leadership will want to see how this fits into what we're already doing. I can help with that conversation if needed. Alright, I think we're ready to move forward. Let's check in tomorrow on progress?
Sounds good. I'll get started on A1 today and have something to share by tomorrow. Thanks everyone for the clarity on direction.
Great. I'll have a first draft of T2 and A2 by EOD tomorrow. Let's reconvene in this thread once we have those docs ready for feedback.

threads.thread_goal: Review and finalise the early identification and referral protocol and observation checklist.

messages.text: Hi all, I've drafted the early identification and referral protocol (A2) and it's ready for feedback. The protocol includes: roles for school and social services, step-by-step referral process, consent requirements, and data protection safeguards. I've also reviewed it against T11 to make sure it aligns with existing school procedures. Can everyone take a look and share thoughts? Particularly interested in whether the steps are clear and realistic for daily use.

Thanks for getting this out. I've read through it and it looks solid. One question: the consent section—do we need separate consent for the initial referral and then again for home visits? Or is one consent form enough? Also, I've drafted the observation checklist (A3) and it covers behaviour, learning, and safety indicators. It's designed to take about 5 minutes per child. Can you review it for alignment with the protocol?

Good question on consent. I think we need two separate consents: one for the initial referral and information sharing, and a second one if we're planning a home visit. That's clearer for families and safer legally. Let me review A3 and get back to you. 511446, can you also check the checklist for practicality in the classroom?

I've looked at A3 and it's good. The indicators are clear and the format is easy to use. One thing: we should make sure teachers know when to use it—is it weekly, or only when we suspect a child needs support? That'll affect how we roll it out. Also, the protocol looks comprehensive, but I want to make sure the language is accessible for all staff, not just social workers.

Good point on language. I've been reading through A2 and there are a few terms that might confuse classroom staff—like 'safeguarding threshold' and 'data controller'. Can we simplify those? Also, on the checklist timing: I'd suggest we use it for all children at the start of the pilot, just to get a baseline. Then we can adjust based on what we learn.

Fair point. I'll simplify the language in A2. And I like the idea of using the checklist for all children initially—that gives us good data and avoids singling anyone out. Let me revise both documents and share a second draft by tomorrow. 499701, can you also check that the checklist aligns with what teachers will actually see in the classroom?

I'll review it again with that lens. I'm also thinking about T3—the definition of done says the checklist needs to be approved by a social worker for relevance. 361403, once you've revised A2, can you confirm that A3 covers the right indicators from a social work perspective?

Absolutely. I'll review A3 for social work relevance and sign off on it. I think we're close. Let me get the revised A2 out by EOD tomorrow, and then we can lock in both documents. Once we do, we'll have D3 and D4 confirmed—protocol approved and checklist finalized.

Sounds good. I'll also make sure the checklist is ready for the two pilot classes. One more thing: should we include a section in the protocol about what happens if a child is in immediate danger? That's a safeguarding priority.

Excellent catch. Yes, I'll add a section on urgent safeguarding concerns—that needs to bypass the normal referral process and go straight to the safeguarding lead. I'll include that in the revised A2.
Good. That's critical. I think once we have the revised A2 and A3, we should do a quick review with school leadership to make sure everything aligns with T11. I can help coordinate that.

Perfect. Let's plan for that review by end of week. I'll have the revised documents ready by tomorrow EOD, and 350111 can set up a quick check-in with leadership. Once we get their sign-off, we can finalize D3 and D4.

threads.thread_goal: Define classroom support routines and align them with school procedures and workload.

messages.text: Hi team, I've drafted some classroom support routines for at-risk children (A4). These are practical strategies we can use daily without overloading teachers. I've included: buddy systems, quiet work spaces, check-in time with an adult, visual schedules, and positive reinforcement routines. Each one is designed to fit into existing classroom management. But I want to be honest: I'm not sure if these are realistic given how busy our days are. Can you give me feedback on whether this is doable?

I've reviewed A4 and I think it's solid. The routines are practical and I've used similar approaches. The buddy system and check-in time are especially good because they don't require extra prep. One thing: we should make sure these align with our curriculum objectives—that way teachers see them as supporting learning, not just behaviour management. Have you checked that against T6?

Good point. From a social work angle, I'd add one more: a simple way for children to communicate when they're struggling—maybe a signal or a safe person to talk to. That supports emotional wellbeing, which is part of what we're trying to achieve. Also, I want to make sure these routines don't add stress to staff. Can we keep the list to 5–6 strategies max?

I like that idea about communication. And yes, keeping it to 5–6 is smart. I'm a bit worried about the workload piece though. We're already stretched thin, and adding new routines could feel like one more thing. How do we make sure teachers actually use these without it becoming a burden? Maybe we need to think about T10—the feedback loop—so we can adjust if something isn't working.

That's fair. I think the key is to frame these as replacements for things we're already doing, not additions. For example, the buddy system replaces random pairing; the check-in time replaces informal chats. If we position it that way, it might feel less like extra work. And yes, T10 is crucial—we need to check in weekly with staff and adjust based on what's working.

I like that framing. It makes it feel more manageable. I'd also suggest we document these routines in a simple one-page guide—something teachers can print and keep at their desk. That way they don't have to remember everything. Should that be part of A4?

Absolutely. A4 should include a one-page quick reference guide. And I want to make sure we also document how these routines support social-emotional development—that's part of T6. Once we finalize the list, I can review it from a wellbeing perspective and confirm it aligns with what we're trying to achieve.

Good. So here's what I'm hearing: we narrow the list to 5–6 strategies, add a communication/emotional support element, create a one-page guide, and make sure it aligns with curriculum and wellbeing goals. I can revise A4 with all of that by tomorrow. Then we need to think about how to store and share this with staff—that's part of D6.

On storage and access: I'd suggest a shared folder that everyone can access, plus a printed copy in each classroom. That way it's easy to reference during the day. We could also include it in the training materials. Should that be part of A8—the feedback process?

Yes, A8 should include how staff access the routines guide. And we should also include a simple feedback form—something like 'What's working?' and 'What's not?'—so we can gather input weekly. That ties into T10. I think we're getting close to D5 and D6.

I think we're ready. Let me summarize: we're going with 5–6 support strategies, including a communication element. A4 will include a one-page guide and alignment with curriculum and wellbeing. A8 will explain how staff access the guide and provide a feedback form. Does that capture D5 and D6?
Yes, that's it. I'll revise A4 by tomorrow and include the one-page guide. 361403, can you review it for the wellbeing angle? And 350111, can you draft the access and feedback section for A8?

I can do that. I'll draft the access and feedback section for A8 by tomorrow. One thing I want to flag: we should also think about how to train staff on these routines. That's part of T7. Should we include a demo or walkthrough in the training?

Definitely. T7 should include a demo of the routines so staff can see them in action. I'll make sure that's part of the training plan. Alright, I think we have a solid plan. Let's reconvene once we have the revised A4 and A8.
Great. I'll have A4 ready by EOD tomorrow. Thanks everyone for the feedback—this is much more realistic now.

threads.thread_goal: Agree on family engagement approach and home visit criteria.

messages.text: Hi all, I've drafted the family engagement script and home visit criteria (A5 and T5). The script is designed to be warm and clear—explaining the programme without jargon. The home visit criteria define when a visit is recommended and include safety procedures. I want to make sure this feels right for families and is realistic for our team. Can you review and give feedback?

I've read through A5 and it's good. The language is accessible and the tone is supportive. One thing: I'd suggest we also include information about what parents can expect—like, how often will we be in touch? What will we share with them? That might help with buy-in. Also, on T5: the home visit criteria look reasonable, but I'm wondering about the timing. How do we fit home visits into our schedules?

Good questions. On the timing: the project constraints say we have limited availability for home visits outside core working hours. So we need to be realistic about when visits can happen. Maybe we should prioritize visits for families who are hardest to reach, and do phone or school-based meetings for others?

That's smart. I'll revise T5 to include flexible options: home visits for priority cases, phone calls for others, and school-based meetings as a third option. That way we're not overcommitting. And I'll add to A5 what families can expect in terms of contact frequency and what we'll share. I think that addresses the buy-in concern.

I like that approach. One more thing: we should make sure the script includes a clear explanation of confidentiality and consent. Parents need to know what information we're sharing and with whom. That ties back to the protocol we finalized in TH2.

Absolutely. I'll add a section to A5 about confidentiality and consent—keeping it simple and clear. And I'll make sure T5 includes safety procedures for home visits, like always going in pairs and letting someone know where we are.
Good. Safety is non-negotiable. I'd also suggest we include a section in T5 about what to do if a family declines a home visit or is hard to reach. We need a plan for that.

Good point. I'll add that to T5. So here's the plan: I'll revise A5 to include contact frequency, confidentiality, and consent information. I'll revise T5 to include flexible contact options, safety procedures, and a plan for families who decline or are hard to reach. Can everyone review the revised versions by tomorrow?

I'll review. One more thing: should we also think about how to communicate this to families? Like, do we send the leaflet home first, or do we talk to them in person? That might affect how we roll out the programme.

Good question. I think we should do both: send the leaflet home first so families have time to read it, then follow up with a conversation—either in person or by phone. That gives them a chance to ask questions. I'll include that in the communication plan for A5.
That makes sense. And we should make sure the leaflet is available in different languages if needed. That's part of being inclusive and accessible.
Absolutely. I'll note that in A5. Alright, I think we're close to D7 and D8. Let me get the revised versions out by EOD tomorrow, and we can finalize both decisions.
Sounds good. I'll review the revised versions and give feedback. I think once we have D7 and D8 locked in, we'll be ready to move into the training and pilot planning phase.
Agreed. Let's reconvene once we have the revised A5 and T5. Thanks for pulling this together, 361403.

threads.thread_goal: Lock in monitoring indicators, reporting template, and pilot start date.

messages.text: Hi all, I've drafted the monitoring and reporting template (A6) and proposed indicators for evaluating the pilot (T12). The template includes sections for wellbeing, learning, and safety. The indicators are: attendance, observed wellbeing, incidents, and engagement in support routines. I want to make sure these are realistic to track and that the template is easy for both school and social work staff to use. Can you review?

I've looked at A6 and it's clear. The sections make sense and the fields are straightforward. On T12: the indicators are good, but I'm wondering about 'observed wellbeing'—how do we measure that consistently? Maybe we need a simple scale or description to make it more objective?

Good point. I'd suggest a simple three-point scale: 'struggling', 'managing', 'thriving'. That's easy to use and gives us consistent data. Also, on A6: I want to make sure the data protection section is clear. Staff need to know how to store and who can access the information.

Good suggestions. I'll add the three-point scale to T12 and include clear data protection notes in A6. I'll also add a section on who can access the template and how it should be stored. That ties back to the protocol we finalized.

I think that's good. One thing: we should also think about how often we review the data. Weekly? Monthly? That'll affect how much work it is for staff. And we need to decide who's responsible for collecting and summarizing the data.

Good questions. I'd suggest we review the data weekly during the pilot—that's frequent enough to catch issues but not overwhelming. And I think the responsibility should be shared: school staff collect data on their end, social work staff on theirs, and we meet weekly to review together. I'll add that to T12.

That works. Weekly reviews will also help us catch problems early and adjust the programme if needed. Now, on the pilot start date: we've been working on this for about a week. Do we have everything ready to start? Or do we need more time?

Let me check: we have A2 and A3 finalized, A4 and A8 ready, A5 and T5 ready, and now A6 and T12. We still need T7 (training plan) and we need to finalize A7 (pilot plan and schedule). I think we can start the pilot in about 5 days if we move quickly on those last two items.

Five days is tight but doable. We need to make sure staff are trained before we start, so T7 is critical. I can help with that if needed. And we should confirm with school leadership that we're ready to go.

I'll coordinate with school leadership. But I want to flag: we're moving fast, and I'm a bit concerned about whether we've thought through all the details. Are we sure the two pilot classes are ready? Do the teachers understand what's expected?

Fair point. Let me revise: we should do a quick check-in with the pilot class teachers before we start. That's part of T7—the training. I'll make sure the training includes a walkthrough of what to expect and a chance for teachers to ask questions. That should address the readiness concern.

Good. So here's the timeline: we finalize A6 and T12 by tomorrow, we draft T7 by the day after, and we finalize A7 by end of week. Then we do the training with pilot class teachers, and we start the pilot early next week. Does that work?
Yes, that works. I'll finalize A6 and T12 by tomorrow, and I'll draft T7 by the day after. 350111, can you finalize A7 and coordinate with school leadership?
I can do that. I'll finalize A7 by end of week and set up a meeting with school leadership to confirm the pilot start date and get their sign-off.
Great. I think we're on track. Once we have all the materials ready, we should do a final review to make sure everything is aligned. Then we can move into the training and pilot phase.

Agreed. Let me also reconfirm D1 and D3 at this point: we're going with 2–3 pilot classes, starting early next week, and the protocol is approved pending any final tweaks from the monitoring needs. Does everyone agree?
Yes, I agree. I think we've done solid work here. Let's get the final materials ready and move into the pilot.
